newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end powerhouse rally.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end powerhouse rally.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed lower Thursday, snapping a three-session winning streak that saw the Dow climb nearly 290 points in a powerhouse rally.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended 21.27 points lower at 6,658.60. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,295 to 1,185 on active volume of 502 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Dow's performance since Monday was paralleled in recent history only by a 289-point surge in the two days after the "Black Monday" market crash of 1987.
"The market seemed a little tired today," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Once again, the market turned in a mixed performance, but this time it was technology shares that rallied as blue chips fell victim to profit-taking.
"Techs had dramatically lagged and today it was like someone finally said it was O.K. to buy techs," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.
Analysts said much of the buying in technology and other sectors appeared focused on the top tier names, which they said was evidence the market remained on edge.
"This rally has been as narrow as any we've seen this year," Bleier said. "The money coming in is seeking out the very top names."
A strong bond market boosted interest-rate-sensitive sectors like transportation and finance.
The 30-year Treasury bond rose 12/32, lowering its yield to 7.07 percent from Wednesday's close of 7.10 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
Bonds reacted to a weaker-than-expected report on regional business activity from the Philadelphia Federal Reserve.
While the data did not eliminate market tension over the chances of another interest rate increase, analysts said it did offer at least some evidence that economic growth may be moderating.
"The Philly Fed numbers show some signs of slowdown in the manufacturing sector, and that's a good thing," said Bill Meehan, analyst at Prudential Securities.
BankAmerica Corp. rose 2-3/4 to 106-5/8 and Citicorp gained 1-1/8 to 105-1/2. United Airlines parent company UAL Corp. added 1-5/8 to 74-5/8 and Delta Air Lines Inc. climbed 1-1/2 to 92-3/8.
American Airlines parent company AMR Corp. rose 2-1/2 to 87-1/2. AMR's stronger-than-expected first quarter earnings, reported on Wednesday, also were cited as a factor in the rise of airline shares.
Earnings dominated much of the session and investors again pummeled companies whose growth outlooks are in question.
Footstar Inc. tumbled 6-1/2 to 18-5/8 despite announcing first-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street estimates. The company warned it saw signs of slower sales trends in the athletic sector.
Andrew Corp. slid 12-1/8 to 23-1/2 after the telecommunications equipment company's second quarter sales growth failed to match analysts' expectations.
Raychem Corp. skidded 12-1/2 to 68-7/8. Raychem cautioned late Wednesday that it expected currency fluctuations would hurt its near-term results.
Cyrix Corp. jumped 3-7/8 to 21-5/8 after the computer chip maker reported first quarter net income that far surpassed Wall Street expectations.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 6.80 points to 1,217.07.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 1.76 points to 761.77. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.99 to 555.52.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 1.10 to 400.65. The average share was down 11 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,233.561 down 9.429 or 0.13 percent.
